<issue>
Stateless streamable HTTP: tools/call with progress returns notification as response body
Part of #977.

On the 2026-07-28 suite (`0.2.0-alpha.9`), `tools-call-with-progress` fails against the stateless conformance server:

```
Failed: HTTP 200: expected a JSON-RPC result for 'tools/call', got unexpected body
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/progress","params":{"message":"Starting","progress":0,"progressToken":"progress-test-1","total":100}}
```

In stateless mode the progress notification is emitted as the POST response body instead of (or before) the final `tools/call` result. The scenario passes against the stateful server on the 2025-11-25 suite, so this is specific to the stateless lifecycle.

Repro:

```bash
cargo build -p mcp-conformance
STATELESS=1 PORT=8002 ./target/debug/conformance-server &
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.9 server \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp \
  --scenario tools-call-with-progress -o results
```

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Rust rmcp repo), find the stateless streamable HTTP server handling of POST requests (likely crates/rmcp/src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs, look for json_response / stateless). Report the code of the stateless POST request branch in full with line numbers, including how it handles messages from the service (notifications vs response).

content.content: {"summary":"The stateless POST branch is in crates/rmcp/src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs, inside the POST handler, lines 1559-1667 (`match message`). Requests run through a one-shot service with a per-request cancellation token. With json_response it returns JSON when the first message is a Response or Error, and otherwise falls back to SSE. Notifications and client Responses/Errors get an immediate 'accepted' reply. The full verbatim listing was not included here because the required output format is JSON only; the key lines are quoted below.","findings":["tower.rs:1559 `match message {` dispatches on ClientJsonRpcMessage.","tower.rs:1560-1588 Request arm: if the request negotiates a per-request version (has_per_request_version or DiscoverRequest), it calls serve_negotiated_request_directly (1562-1565). Otherwise it builds peer_info, inserts the http parts into extensions, and creates a OneshotTransport plus a fresh request_ct CancellationToken. It then calls serve_directly_with_ct and spawns service.waiting().","tower.rs:1589 `if self.config.json_response {` takes the JSON branch. It races receiver.recv() against the cancellation token, with a drop_guard on request_ct that is disarmed once a message arrives. A None result returns internal_error_response(\"empty response\").","tower.rs:1600-1611 If the first message is ServerJsonRpcMessage::Response(_) or ::Error(_), it is serialized with serde_json and returned as 200 OK with the JSON_MIME_TYPE content type.","tower.rs:1612-1627 Otherwise (intermediate notification or request), it falls back to SSE. It chains the first message with ReceiverStream(receiver) through CancelOnDisconnect(request_ct), so the full message sequence is preserved.","tower.rs:1645-1656 `} else {` is SSE mode (default). The ReceiverStream is wrapped in CancelOnDisconnect(stream, request_ct) and returned via sse_stream_response.","tower.rs:1661-1663 ClientJsonRpcMessage::Notification(_notification) => ignored, returns accepted_response() (202-style accepted, no body).","tower.rs:1665 ClientJsonRpcMessage::Response(_json_rpc_response) => Ok(accepted_response()).","tower.rs:1666 ClientJsonRpcMessage::Error(_json_rpc_error) => Ok(accepted_response())."],"confidence":0.85}

input.instruction: In /testbed, look at conformance server crate (mcp-conformance, bin conformance-server) and how STATELESS env configures StreamableHttpServerConfig (json_response, stateful_mode). Report the relevant code with line numbers.

content.content: {"summary":"The conformance-server binary (package mcp-conformance) reads the STATELESS env var; if it is set (any value, presence only), it turns off stateful_mode and turns on json_response in StreamableHttpServerConfig. Otherwise the rmcp defaults apply (stateful, SSE responses). No files were modified.","findings":["conformance/Cargo.toml:2 package name = \"mcp-conformance\"; :7-9 [[bin]] name = \"conformance-server\", path = src/bin/server.rs","conformance/src/bin/server.rs:1230 `let stateless = std::env::var_os(\"STATELESS\").is_some();` (presence-only check, any value counts)","conformance/src/bin/server.rs:1231-1233 config = StreamableHttpServerConfig::default().with_stateful_mode(!stateless).with_json_response(stateless)","conformance/src/bin/server.rs:1235-1239 StreamableHttpService::new(..., LocalSessionManager::default().into(), config); router nests it at /mcp","conformance/src/bin/server.rs:1222-1228 PORT env (default 8001), binds 127.0.0.1","crates/rmcp/src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs:61-67 fields stateful_mode (bool) and json_response (bool) with doc comments","tower.rs:128-134 Default: stateful_mode: true, json_response: false","tower.rs:179-186 builder methods with_stateful_mode / with_json_response","tower.rs:894 json_response used to choose JSON vs SSE for simple responses; :1161-1165 allowed methods/dispatch depend on stateful_mode; :1343 stateful_mode branch; :1589 json_response branch in response handling"],"confidence":0.9}
